executive_summary:
The single most expensive issue at gingerpeople.com right now is that the storefront is not reachable by automated clients at all. Every surface the harness requested — homepage, /cart, robots.txt and sitemap.xml — returned an HTTP 403 'Just a moment...' Cloudflare bot-management challenge instead of page content. That means this audit could not observe any product, pricing, or merchandising detail; what follows is an access-and-infrastructure audit, and a content-level CRO audit requires an unblocked (real-browser) crawl.

This is not a cosmetic finding. An interactive bot challenge that returns 403 to non-JavaScript clients blocks search-engine and social-preview crawlers (hurting organic discovery and link previews), blocks the emerging class of AI shopping and comparison agents (hurting agentic-commerce demand), blocks accessibility scanners and link/uptime monitors, and adds a pre-paint interstitial that can raise bounce for real human visitors on slow or privacy-restricted browsers. Returning, high-intent sessions arriving via email, SMS, retargeting, or affiliate deep links to /cart hit the same wall — a silent loss of the most valuable traffic.

The experiments below span all five pillars, but they are deliberately framed around the access barrier and its measurable revenue consequences, with honestly modest confidence because no page content was observable. The priority is to make verified crawlers, agents, and returning human sessions pass through protection cleanly; once the store is observable again, re-run the harness to produce the content-level Conversion/AOV/Retention experiments this brand likely warrants.

experiments.title: Allow verified search and AI agents through bot protection

evidence.note: Homepage returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interactive challenge instead of HTML, so non-browser clients cannot read the page.

experiments.hypothesis: Organic and agentic discovery improves by letting verified search engines, social-preview bots, and AI shopping agents reach real HTML, because every non-JavaScript client is currently served a 403 challenge and sees no content.
experiments.primary_change: Configure the WAF to allow-list verified crawler/agent traffic and serve real page HTML to them instead of the interactive challenge.
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if indexed pages and organic impressions rise without a measurable increase in abusive bot load.

experiments.title: Make robots.txt and sitemap.xml crawler-reachable

evidence.note: Both sitemap.xml (pg_0fbaca19) and robots.txt (pg_e06b450e) returned 403 challenges, so search engines cannot fetch the crawl directives or URL inventory.

experiments.hypothesis: Crawl efficiency and indexation improve by exempting robots.txt and sitemap.xml from the challenge, because search engines currently receive a 403 for both and cannot discover the URL set.
experiments.primary_change: Add edge rules that always serve robots.txt and sitemap.xml as plain, un-challenged responses.
experiments.primary_kpi: Pages crawled and indexed per week
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if weekly crawled/indexed pages increase with no rise in malicious sitemap scraping.

experiments.title: Replace the interactive challenge for human traffic

evidence.note: The captured homepage body is the Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial, which runs a JavaScript check before any store content can paint.

experiments.hypothesis: First-visit bounce drops by replacing the interactive 'Just a moment...' interstitial with a lower-friction managed mode for human traffic, because the challenge delays first contentful paint on every cold visit.
experiments.primary_change: Switch human traffic from an interactive challenge to a transparent/managed challenge mode and tune sensitivity to reduce interstitial frequency.
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if entry bounce drops without a meaningful increase in confirmed bot abuse.

experiments.title: Stop the /cart edge from returning a challenge

evidence.note: The /cart URL returned a 403 'Just a moment...' challenge rather than a cart or recovery page.

experiments.hypothesis: High-intent session loss drops by ensuring /cart resolves to a real cart or recovery page for human sessions, because a 403 challenge at the cart URL strands returning users, tracking links, and partner referrals.
experiments.primary_change: Ensure /cart bypasses the interactive challenge for human sessions and returns the cart or a branded recovery page with continue-shopping and support links.
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if /cart exit rate drops without hurting site-wide conversion.

experiments.title: Recover returning sessions blocked at entry

evidence.note: Inferred from the 403 challenge on /cart, the most common deep-link destination for returning and retargeted users.

experiments.hypothesis: Returning-visitor conversion improves by letting recognized returning sessions skip the interactive challenge, because high-intent users arriving via retargeting and cart deep links currently hit a 403 wall before they can transact.
experiments.primary_change: Allow-list authenticated/returning sessions (clearance cookie or first-party signal) so they reach the store without an interactive challenge.
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if returning-visitor conversion improves without a rise in fraudulent sessions.

experiments.title: Provide a no-JavaScript fallback to browse and buy

evidence.note: The only content served to a non-JS client was the 'Just a moment...' challenge, so JS-disabled, privacy-browser, and some assistive-tech users see no store.

experiments.hypothesis: Conversion among privacy-browser and assistive-technology users improves by offering a no-JavaScript fallback path to the catalog and buy flow, because such users currently receive only the challenge interstitial.
experiments.primary_change: Serve a progressively-enhanced fallback so core catalog browsing and add-to-cart work without passing an interactive JavaScript challenge.
experiments.primary_kpi: Conversion rate among no-JS / assistive sessions
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if conversion among no-JS/assistive sessions improves without weakening abuse protection.

experiments.title: Unblock campaign deep links that pre-load carts

evidence.note: Inferred from the 403 on /cart: links that pre-load multi-item carts or bundles land on the same challenged URL.

experiments.hypothesis: Order value from campaign channels rises by exempting known deep-link/cart-permalink entry paths from the interactive challenge, because pre-loaded multi-item carts currently fail at a 403 before checkout.
experiments.primary_change: Exempt verified campaign and cart-permalink entry paths from the interactive challenge so multi-item carts load intact.
experiments.primary_kpi: Average order value from email/affiliate deep-link sessions
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if deep-link-session AOV rises by at least $3 without increasing fraud chargebacks.

experiments.title: Expose an agent-readable product feed

evidence.note: Inferred from the homepage 403: AI shopping and comparison agents that could assemble baskets cannot read the storefront at all.

experiments.hypothesis: Basket revenue from agent and comparison channels rises by publishing an agent-accessible product feed, because every automated assistant that could assemble a multi-item order is currently blocked by the challenge.
experiments.primary_change: Publish a stable, un-challenged structured product feed (and allow-list reputable shopping agents) so assistants can read catalog and price.
experiments.primary_kpi: Orders and AOV attributed to agent/comparison channels
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if agent-channel orders/AOV grow without degrading first-party margins.

experiments.title: Unblock lifecycle email/SMS deep links

evidence.note: Inferred from the 403 on /cart: returning customers clicking lifecycle links to cart/account hit the challenge.

experiments.hypothesis: Repeat purchase rate improves by ensuring lifecycle email/SMS links for returning customers bypass the interactive challenge, because those links currently route high-intent repeat buyers into a 403.
experiments.primary_change: Tag and allow-list lifecycle deep links (and recognized returning sessions) so repeat customers land directly on the intended page.
experiments.primary_kpi: 30-day repeat purchase rate from lifecycle links
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if repeat purchase rate from lifecycle links improves without a rise in link abuse.

experiments.title: Reduce challenge friction on account/login surfaces

evidence.note: Inferred from the site-wide 403 challenge observed on the homepage: returning buyers attempting to log in or reorder face the same interstitial.

experiments.hypothesis: Reorder rate improves by minimizing challenge friction on account/login and reorder surfaces, because returning buyers must clear an interactive challenge before they can authenticate and repurchase.
experiments.primary_change: Prioritize recognized returning/authenticated sessions through protection with minimal friction on login and reorder paths.
experiments.decision_rule: Ship if login-to-reorder completion improves without weakening account-takeover defenses.
